Environmental values inside points, buffers and areas

Source: vignettes/workflow-values-in-shapes.Rmd
workflow-values-in-shapes.Rmd

This article shows how to get environmental values inside 3D shapes, such as tag detections, buffers around them, or a protected area down to a set depth. Each example uses the same three steps:

  1. Build the shapes with as_vector3d() or buffer_3d().
  2. Intersect each shape with the data: crop() the dataset to the shape, read its time steps with as_voxel(), and keep the values inside the shape with mask().
  3. Summarise the values with summarise_3d().

You loop over the shapes yourself, so you can stop after any step and look at the result. Each example ends with a table of values per shape, which you can join back to your observations. Volumes are in km³ throughout.

Example data

The examples use a small synthetic temperature dataset: a 0.05° grid off eastern Australia, six depth levels from 0 to 200 m, and five daily time steps. Temperature falls with depth, rises to the north and warms a little each day. The code below writes it to a netCDF file, as you might download from Copernicus Marine.

library(ocean3d)

lon <- seq(150.025, 150.975, by = 0.05)
lat <- seq(-20.975, -20.025, by = 0.05)
depth <- c(0, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200)
time <- 0:4
grid <- expand.grid(lon = lon, lat = lat, depth = depth, time = time)
temp <- 28 - 0.06 * grid$depth + 2 * (grid$lat + 20.5) + 0.2 * grid$time

dims <- list(
  ncdf4::ncdim_def("lon", "degrees_east", lon),
  ncdf4::ncdim_def("lat", "degrees_north", lat),
  ncdf4::ncdim_def("depth", "m", depth),
  ncdf4::ncdim_def("time", "days since 2020-03-01", time)
)
var <- ncdf4::ncvar_def("temp", "degC", dims, missval = -9999,
                        prec = "double")
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".nc")
nc <- ncdf4::nc_create(path, var)
ncdf4::ncvar_put(nc, var, array(temp, lengths(lapply(dims, `[[`, "vals"))))
ncdf4::nc_close(nc)

as_proxy() describes the file without reading its values. Each later step reads only the cells and time steps it needs, at every depth level.

proxy <- as_proxy(path)
proxy
#> class      : SpatProxy (experimental)
#> source     : file22a9108c62f.nc
#> variable   : temp (degC)
#> dimensions : 20 x 20 x 6 x 5 (lon x lat x depth x time)
#> lon        : 150.025 to 150.975, 20 cells, edges inferred
#> lat        : -20.975 to -20.025, 20 cells, edges inferred
#> depth      : 0 to 200 m, 6 levels, shallow first, edges inferred
#> time       : 2020-03-01 to 2020-03-05, 5 steps, standard calendar, no bounds
#> crs        : EPSG:4326

Points: tag detections

Three detections, each with a position, a depth and a date, become SpatVector3D points:

obs <- data.frame(
  tag = c("A", "B", "C"),
  lon = c(150.21, 150.52, 150.80),
  lat = c(-20.31, -20.56, -20.82),
  depth = c(12, 48, 140),
  date = as.Date(c("2020-03-01", "2020-03-02", "2020-03-04"))
)
detections <- as_vector3d(obs, time = "date", id = "tag")
detections
#> class      : SpatVector3D
#> geometry   : points 
#> features   : 3 
#> vertices   : 3 
#> depth (m)  : 12 to 140 
#> time       : 2020-03-01 to 2020-03-04

For one detection, crop() keeps the grid cell it falls in, and as_voxel() reads the time step nearest its date. With a shape as time, as_voxel() always returns a list, here with one voxel. mask() then keeps the value at the depth level nearest the detection’s depth:

a <- detections[1]
v <- as_voxel(crop(proxy, a), time = a)[[1]]
summarise_3d(mask(v, a), statistic = "mean")
#>         time  mean n
#> 1 2020-03-01 27.75 1

Detection A at 12 m takes the 10 m level. extract_to_point() gives the same value from the file:

extract_to_point(obs[1, ], path, var = "temp", date_col = "date",
                 method = "nearest")$temp
#> [1] 27.75

Both pick the nearest time step: on this data they give the same values for all three detections, for a time halfway between two steps, and for a date after the last step. extract_to_point() warns when the step it picks is on another day; as_voxel() doesn’t, so set max_time_diff in as_voxel() to limit how far away the step may be.

The two differ when the nearest depth level has no value. extract_to_point() skips depth levels with no value when it looks for the nearest one. mask() uses the nearest level whatever its value, so such a detection gets NA.

Buffers: the water around each detection

buffer_3d() turns each detection into a polygon: here a circle of 5 km radius, from 20 m above to 20 m below the detection, and one day either side.

buffers <- buffer_3d(detections, radius_km = 5, depth_window = 20,
                     time_window = 1)
as.data.frame(buffers)[c("feature_id", "depth_min", "depth_max",
                         "time_start", "time_end")]
#>   feature_id depth_min depth_max time_start   time_end
#> 1          A         0        32 2020-02-29 2020-03-02
#> 2          B        28        68 2020-03-01 2020-03-03
#> 3          C       120       160 2020-03-03 2020-03-05

The steps are the same as for one detection, run for each buffer in turn. as_voxel() returns one voxel for each time step inside a buffer’s window: three for B and C, and two for A, whose window starts before the first day of data. Given that list of voxels, summarise_3d() gives one row per time step. By default the mean is weighted by the volume of water each value stands for, and n counts the values used.

mask() uses only a buffer’s outline and depth range, because as_voxel() has already used its time. It prints a message saying so each time, which suppressMessages() hides inside the loop.

buffer_rows <- lapply(seq_along(buffers), function(i) {
  b <- buffers[i]
  voxels <- as_voxel(crop(proxy, b), time = b)
  inside <- lapply(voxels, function(v) suppressMessages(mask(v, b)))
  rows <- summarise_3d(inside, statistic = c("mean", "sd"))
  cbind(feature_id = as.data.frame(b)$feature_id, rows)
})
do.call(rbind, buffer_rows)
#>   feature_id       time     mean        sd  n
#> 1          A 2020-03-01 27.36252 0.5863953 24
#> 2          A 2020-03-02 27.56252 0.5863953 24
#> 3          B 2020-03-01 25.38426 0.7445443 16
#> 4          B 2020-03-02 25.58426 0.7445443 16
#> 5          B 2020-03-03 25.78426 0.7445443 16
#> 6          C 2020-03-03 18.32145 3.1053138 12
#> 7          C 2020-03-04 18.52145 3.1053138 12
#> 8          C 2020-03-05 18.72145 3.1053138 12

Each row summarises one time step; summarise_3d() doesn’t pool values across steps.

Areas: a protected area down to 50 m

An area is a polygon with a depth range. This one covers the middle of the grid, from the surface to 50 m:

mpa <- sf::st_sf(
  name = "reef",
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(
    c(150.3, -20.7), c(150.7, -20.7), c(150.7, -20.3), c(150.3, -20.3),
    c(150.3, -20.7)
  ))), crs = 4326)
)
reef <- as_vector3d(mpa, depth_min = 0, depth_max = 50)
volume(reef) # km³
#> [1] 92.38822

The area has no time, so pick the time step with a date. by = "depth" gives one row per depth level:

v <- as_voxel(crop(proxy, reef), time = "2020-03-03")
summarise_3d(mask(v, reef), statistic = c("mean", "min", "max"),
             by = "depth")
#>         time depth     mean   min   max  n
#> 1 2020-03-03     0 28.40017 28.05 28.75 64
#> 2 2020-03-03    10 27.80017 27.45 28.15 64
#> 3 2020-03-03    25 26.90017 26.55 27.25 64
#> 4 2020-03-03    50 25.40017 25.05 25.75 64
#> 5 2020-03-03   100       NA    NA    NA  0
#> 6 2020-03-03   200       NA    NA    NA  0

The 50 m level counts because the water it stands for, from 37.5 m to 75 m, overlaps the area’s depth range; vignette("depth-levels") describes this rule. The 100 m and 200 m levels are outside the area, so their rows have NA and n = 0.

Through time: habitat volume per day

volume() on the proxy measures each time step in turn, in km³. Pass fun to count only some values as habitat, here water between 24 and 26 °C:

volume(proxy, fun = function(x) x >= 24 & x <= 26)
#>         time volume_km3
#> 1 2020-03-01   490.6675
#> 2 2020-03-02   424.1851
#> 3 2020-03-03   357.7448
#> 4 2020-03-04   302.8561
#> 5 2020-03-05   259.5079

The habitat shrinks from day to day because the synthetic water warms each day.

For the habitat inside the area only, keep the habitat in one day’s voxel with occupied(). Masking it by the area would keep whole depth levels, so the 50 m level would count water down to 75 m, below the area’s floor. Instead, turn the habitat into a depth range per cell with voxel_to_envelope() and intersect it with the area, which cuts it at 50 m:

habitat <- occupied(v, function(x) x >= 24 & x <= 26)
inside <- intersect_3d(voxel_to_envelope(habitat), reef)
volume(inside) # km³
#> [1] 23.097

Putting the rows together

The buffer loop ends with a list of data frames, one per buffer, each starting with the buffer’s feature_id. do.call(rbind, ...) joins them into one table, which you can then join back to the observations by ID. In the result, date is the detection date and time is the time step the values come from:

results <- do.call(rbind, buffer_rows)
merge(obs, results, by.x = "tag", by.y = "feature_id")
#>   tag    lon    lat depth       date       time     mean        sd  n
#> 1   A 150.21 -20.31    12 2020-03-01 2020-03-01 27.36252 0.5863953 24
#> 2   A 150.21 -20.31    12 2020-03-01 2020-03-02 27.56252 0.5863953 24
#> 3   B 150.52 -20.56    48 2020-03-02 2020-03-01 25.38426 0.7445443 16
#> 4   B 150.52 -20.56    48 2020-03-02 2020-03-02 25.58426 0.7445443 16
#> 5   B 150.52 -20.56    48 2020-03-02 2020-03-03 25.78426 0.7445443 16
#> 6   C 150.80 -20.82   140 2020-03-04 2020-03-03 18.32145 3.1053138 12
#> 7   C 150.80 -20.82   140 2020-03-04 2020-03-04 18.52145 3.1053138 12
#> 8   C 150.80 -20.82   140 2020-03-04 2020-03-05 18.72145 3.1053138 12
